Subject: Renewal PO & short-term price hold request

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing the purchase order for our July renewal and working through the internal procurement checklist. Two asks from our side before we route to finance:

1) Can Redwood hold current rates for 90 days post-renewal while we complete a regional migration (we'll be shifting some traffic to EU regions in Q3)?
2) We expect usage to ramp sooner than our committed tier — can we discuss a temporary volume reshuffle (move 25% of Q3 burst to Q2) and a bridging credit to smooth the invoice?

I've attached the latest MOA draft and our projected usage for Q2/Q3. If you can confirm the PO wording and the short-term price hold option, we can push this through legal this week.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Integrations
Silvanet

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. We're aligned to move quickly on this. High-level response below; I'll coordinate internally for the formal PO language.

Summary of asks (for clarity):
- 90-day rate hold post-renewal while you migrate regionally
- Volume reshuffle: shift ~25% of expected Q3 burst to Q2 and provide a bridging credit

Internal next steps: looping in Ben and Marissa for pricing/credit approval, and Priyom for contract wording.

Proposed interim terms (pending internal sign-off):
- Price hold: we can offer a 90-day rate hold on current unit rates if the customer signs the current MOA without changes to data residency commitments.
- Bridging credit: a one-time credit equal to 8% of the incremental token usage moved from Q3 to Q2 (applies to consumption above your committed tier), issued as a September credit on the invoice following migration completion.
- Commit reshuffle: convert the requested 25% burst shift into a temporary true-up window (Q2 true-up to count toward Q3 committed volume), with the standard true-up reconciliation at renewal.

Please confirm these high-level points and I'll come back with exact PO wording and a DocuSign envelope.

Best,

Thanks for pulling this together, Tessa. Quick internal take.

Pricing & credits (approved in principle):
- 90-day rate hold: approved conditioned on the MOA remaining with existing residency clauses (no new data cross-border commitments). This is time-limited and non-recurring.
- Bridging credit: offer a one-time credit capped at $45,000 (whichever is lower: 8% of moved incremental usage or cap). Purpose is smoothing operational cashflow while Silvanet migrates.
- Commit reshuffle: accept temporary true-up mechanism where Q2 usage counts toward Q3 commit up to the reshuffled amount (25%). Any overage beyond the reshuffle will be billed at the standard overage rate.

Operational notes (Marissa / Priyom):
- Marissa: update renewal terms doc to include explicit language about the true-up window, invoice timing for the credit, and the 90-day hold.
- Priyom: prepare a brief amendment (one-pager) that can be attached to the MOA and sent via DocuSign.

I'll hold the discount ask for now — we shouldn't change list pricing but the credit + cap should be sufficient operationally for them. If they push for a transient % discount, bring back to me.

Subject: Final terms and PO routing instructions

Alex — appreciate the quick turn. Per internal approvals below, we can proceed with the following binding terms to attach to the PO: 

1) 90-day rate hold: Redwood will hold current unit rates for 90 calendar days following the renewal effective date. This is dependent on sign-off of the current MOA; any changes to data residency will void the hold.
2) Bridging credit: a one-time credit equal to 8% of the moved incremental token usage, capped at $45,000, to be applied to the invoice issued in the September billing cycle after Silvanet confirms migration completion.
3) Commit reshuffle: up to 25% of projected Q3 burst may be reclassified to Q2 for true-up purposes. Reclassified usage will count toward Q3 commit for reconciliation; any additional consumption beyond the reshuffle will be billed at standard overage tier rates.
4) Documentation: attaching the amendment (redwood_renewal_terms_2027.docx) with exact language to be appended to the MOA. DocuSign link will be circulated once you confirm the PO number and signer.

Next steps for Silvanet procurement:
- Confirm PO number and final signer for DocuSign by EOD Monday.
- Once we receive PO number, we will generate DocuSign with the MOA + amendment and provide a clear invoice schedule reflecting the credit application.

Alex — let me know if you need a short call to walk legal/procurement through the amendment. If silence, I'll assume approval and send the DocuSign envelope Monday morning.
